_note: JUDGMENT, not model output: which data belongs to which geographic level. Every level lists what is measured and what is a gap. Edit here, not in app.js.

levels.name: Global
levels.blurb: The world model itself: 12 scenarios, three horizons. This is the only level the model computes natively.

levels.name: Europe
levels.blurb: No European energy model exists here. Eurozone macro series are used as a proxy, and the scenario 'European Restart' is highlighted. Treat as context, not a European forecast.

levels.name: Germany
levels.blurb: The domain lens: how fast can installed renewable capacity become usable, affordable electricity, and which bottleneck decides the pace.

levels.name: Brandenburg
levels.blurb: Measured for Brandenburg: wind and solar capacity in operation, from the federal register of power units (Marktstammdatenregister). Scenarios and indicators are not regional; they come from Germany and the world model.
data_plan: Done: wind and solar capacity in operation by state (Marktstammdatenregister, Bundesnetzagentur)
State-level generation and renewable share (statistical office Berlin-Brandenburg, energy balance)
Districts (Landkreise) with outlines, so the map can compare inside Brandenburg
Grid-connection queue by network operator (primary source still missing, see the Germany GAP)
State industrial production and energy-intensive employment (Destatis regional database)

levels.name: Berlin
levels.blurb: Measured for Berlin: solar capacity on buildings (Marktstammdatenregister) and the yearly peak load at the medium-/low-voltage level (Stromnetz Berlin). Berlin is supplied largely by its surroundings; scenarios and indicators come from Germany and the world model.
